stories.label: Israel's Eisenkot warns Netanyahu against 'dangerous moves' before new government takes office
stories.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming Israel's next government, wrote to caretaker PM Netanyahu warning him not to launch military or security operations without an immediate threat, and told The National Israel should not return to war for now. Lead with the letter: an outgoing prime minister whose wars have killed tens of thousands in Gaza and Lebanon still commands the army during the handover. The mechanism is the caretaker gap; what Eisenkot's own record and coalition mean for Palestinians belongs in the body.

stories.label: CSTO leaders approve nearly 20 documents at Moscow summit
stories.summary: Putin chaired a CSTO summit in the Kremlin that adopted a declaration and 18 other documents, while Al Jazeera frames the meeting as a test of Russia's waning grip on former Soviet allies, with Armenia's absence and distance the clearest sign. Lead with who came and who did not; the mechanism is a security alliance that failed Armenia in 2022-23 and whose Central Asian members (Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan) now hedge toward China and Turkey. Attribute summit outcomes to TASS; Al Jazeera's independent reporting lifts the state-media label.

stories.label: Alexander Darchiev, Russia's Ambassador to the U.S., Dies at 66
stories.summary: Russia's foreign ministry announced the death of Alexander Darchiev, its ambassador in Washington since 2025 and the envoy of the Kremlin-White House rapprochement; no cause was given. Lead with what his post carried: he ran the embassy-normalisation track that preceded the Abu Dhabi talks, and his death leaves that channel without its man in the middle of negotiations. Dateline: Moscow, where the death was announced.

stories.label: Tomás Zambrano, el discípulo de la ultraderecha que tienta a Honduras
stories.summary: Contracorriente reports how Tomás Zambrano, president of Honduras's National Congress since January, opened his term by raising an anti-abortion flag beside the national coat of arms and has set the legislative agenda by the values of the ultraconservative groups he allied with. Lead with the flag and what bills have followed; the mechanism is the far-right network across Central America (Bukele's model, the Próspera lobby) reaching the legislature of the hemisphere's second-poorest country. Dateline: Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: Russian crude oil prices jump on China, India demand
stories.summary: Sanctioned Russian ESPO crude, shipped mainly to Asia, topped $141 a barrel and its premium over Brent hit a record, because China and India, cut off from Gulf barrels by the Hormuz closure, are bidding for Russian oil. Lead with the inversion: sanctions meant to discount Russian oil now coexist with Moscow selling above the benchmark. The mechanism is the war in the Gulf turning Russia into Asia's supplier of last resort. Series: Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Codelco, Adani Group sign pact for copper exploration project
stories.summary: Chile's state copper miner Codelco signed with India's Adani Group to develop the Kaburkaala exploration project in Antofagasta, with Adani financing it in exchange for potential long-term supply to its Mundra smelter. Lead with the trade: Chile's state champion takes capital from an Indian conglomerate under US fraud indictment to secure the metal of electrification. The mechanism is India's push to lock in copper supply outside China's reach. Series: copper. Dateline: Santiago.

stories.label: Fuel prices slashed once again; high-speed diesel cut by Rs7 per litre, petrol by Rs3
stories.summary: Pakistan cut diesel by Rs7 and petrol by Rs3 a litre from 12 November, to Rs364 and Rs335, its latest reduction. Lead with the level: even after the cut, fuel costs a Pakistani worker far more than before the Gulf war, with diesel (which moves food and freight) still above petrol. The mechanism is the fortnightly pricing formula, the petroleum levy the IMF programme requires, and the rupee. Series: Brent crude. Dateline: Islamabad.

stories.label: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, awaits disease-free status
stories.summary: Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient and started the 42-day countdown, to 23 December, before it can be declared free of the disease, Health Minister Aden Duale said. Lead with the countdown and the case and death count; the mechanism is how the outbreak crossed from eastern DR Congo and what contact tracing and vaccination stopped it. Dateline: Nairobi.

stories.label: All of Us study finds thousands of new genetic variants affecting drug responses
stories.summary: A study of nearly 100,000 participants in the NIH's All of Us cohort found thousands of previously unknown variants in the genes that govern how people respond to prescription drugs, because it included ancestries that genetic databases have long left out. Lead with the number and who was missing before; the mechanism is that dosing guidance built on mostly European genomes misses variants common in African, Asian and Latin American ancestry.

stories.label: Scientists Discovered An ‘Invisible’ Object In Space. It’s Challenging Our Understanding of the Cosmos
stories.summary: Astronomers have found an object that emits no detectable light, inferred only from its gravity, which is most likely an ultra-rare supermassive neutron star. Lead with how it was found and its mass; the mechanism is the upper limit on how heavy a neutron star can be before it collapses into a black hole, which this object tests. Name the journal and the team.

stories.label: Scientists find some of the 'very last wild and healthy ecosystems' in the world's oceans untouched by humans
stories.summary: A study in Frontiers in Marine Science found two remote Marshall Islands atolls, Bikar and Bokak, to be among the most intact reef ecosystems left anywhere. Lead with what an untouched reef looks like (predator biomass, coral cover) against the degraded norm; the mechanism is distance from people and fishing, and whether the Marshall Islands, whose own people bear the legacy of US nuclear tests, can protect them. Dateline: Majuro.

stories.label: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50 GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
stories.summary: New York says T-Mobile broke the state law requiring affordable 25 Mbps home internet for low-income households by capping its plan at 50 GB a month and then throttling to 600 kbps, under one-fortieth of the legal speed. Lead with the throttle against the requirement; the mechanism is a carrier meeting the letter of an affordability mandate while making the service unusable for the poorest customers, and what the settlement makes it pay. Dateline: New York.

stories.label: 10秒直出4K图，能画CAD、拆机械，MiniMax这个开源图像模型有点东西
stories.summary: Shanghai's MiniMax released H3-Image with open weights: it renders a 4096x4096 image in about 10 seconds, roughly a fifth of the time of leading closed models, and in Zhidx's tests handled dense Chinese text and 16 reference images at once. Lead with the speed and the open weights; the mechanism is the Chinese labs' open-weight strategy, with commercial licences required above a usage threshold and Nvidia among the licensees of its video model. Dateline: Shanghai.

stories.label: Bessent's relocation: From US to EU, is Iran bringing war to Western soil?
stories.summary: The US Treasury Secretary has been moved onto a military base after death threats, with Bessent, Rubio and Miller reported on an Iranian hit list — the first time the war's retaliation has displaced a sitting cabinet member at home. Lead with the move itself and what it says about how far Tehran's campaign reaches, then tie it to the indictment this week of an Iran-backed network directing attacks on synagogues and US bank buildings in Europe. Distinguish reported threats from proven plots; this is the Iran–US arc the audit is watching.

stories.label: What to know about this year's UN climate talks
stories.summary: New development at COP31 in Antalya: Australia, which leads the negotiations under its deal with host Turkey, is being criticised on the floor for its own fossil-fuel expansion while Guterres warns the climate crisis is 'outrunning us'. Lead with the contradiction of a negotiations chair approving new gas and coal, and who pays for it — the Pacific states Australia claims to speak for. Do not repeat the earlier finance-pledges story; mention it only as context.

stories.label: Israel is 'disrupting entire ecosystems', including Lebanon's wheat crop
stories.summary: Three years of Israeli war on Lebanon have destroyed farmland in the south and the Bekaa Valley, cutting the country's wheat harvest and the livelihoods of farmers who grew it. Lead with the harvest loss in numbers and name who caused it; the mechanism is land made unworkable by strikes and munitions, which outlasts any ceasefire. Wheat prices are a series the site charts; tie the local loss to a country that already imports most of its grain.

stories.label: Stalling for time: Palestinian elections are postponed until next September
stories.summary: Palestinian elections have been pushed back to next September. The question is whether the delay secures a vote that includes Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza under occupation, or just extends the Palestinian Authority's time without an electoral mandate. Lead with the new date and who made the decision, then explain how the occupation controls whether Palestinians in Jerusalem and Gaza can vote at all.

stories.label: Israel Targets U.S. Conservatives in Influence Operation
stories.summary: Starboard, a firm advertising data on 25 million 'verified conservatives', signed a $500,000 agreement to help the State of Israel influence Americans, according to the filed contract. Lead with the dollar figure and the targeting data. The mechanism: a foreign government buying microtargeting of one political constituency, disclosed only through foreign-agent filings. Stick to what the documents show.

stories.label: Mayors, Police, and Prosecutors in Crosshairs as Chile’s Criminal Groups Expand
stories.summary: Chile, long Latin America's safest country, is seeing threats and killings aimed at mayors, police officers and prosecutors as transnational criminal groups expand. This is an early test of President Kast's hardline security agenda. Lead with the count of officials threatened or killed; the mechanism is organised crime moving from fighting rivals to intimidating the state. It also fills a Latin America gap in the audit.

stories.label: Sudan's gold export earnings soar, but the money is not reaching the poor
stories.summary: Sudan's gold exports earned $3.5 billion according to the Ministry of Minerals and the central bank, yet prices keep rising and the economy keeps collapsing for ordinary Sudanese. Lead with the $3.5 billion against the hunger. The mechanism: gold at record prices pays for the war and its commanders, not the population, and it is where the RSF and the army find their money. Gold is a series the site charts.

stories.label: Iran, Oman reach understanding on Hormuz shipping routes -- Iranian parliament speaker
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf says Tehran and Muscat have agreed on the shipping corridor and traffic separation scheme in the Strait of Hormuz, and that the strait 'will not return to what it was before the war'. This is the material new development since today's Rezaei story: a bilateral claim to manage the lanes the world's oil passes through. Attribute it to Russian state news agency TASS and do not state it as fact; Oman has not confirmed it. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Loaded for Bear: SA's GDP and fiscal numbers get a lift from zama zamas
stories.summary: South Africa's twice-a-decade GDP rebasing has made the economy larger on paper, and part of the lift comes from counting illegal artisanal mining, the zama zamas the state also prosecutes. Lead with how much the rebasing added and what it does to debt-to-GDP and the Treasury's fiscal ratios. The mechanism: the same miners the police hunt now help the government's borrowing look cheaper.

stories.label: Trump promises an oil bonanza in Venezuela, but critics question who will benefit
stories.summary: Venezuela's interim president claims the country will earn $200 billion from its oil deal with the US. Critics say billions are being left on the table and the environmental damage in the Orinoco belt is unaddressed. Lead with the $200 billion claim against the terms: who gets the oil, who keeps the revenue, who cleans up. Name the series: Brent crude. Datelined Caracas; it also fills a Latin America gap.

stories.label: IBM to offer access to a dual-processor quantum system in 2027
stories.summary: IBM will link two 520-qubit chips into one system that users can reach before the end of 2027, a step on its roadmap to error-corrected quantum computers before 2030. Lead with the 1,040-qubit linked system and why connecting chips matters more than building ever-larger ones. Explain the mechanism for a technical reader: modular coupling and error correction, and what remains unproven.

stories.label: Gesetz zur digitalen Fairness: Wie die EU Verbraucher im Internet schützen will
stories.summary: The European Commission has proposed its Digital Fairness Act, promising to end subscription traps and manipulative design. It leaves online tracking and data brokerage untouched, and one rule may become the next cookie banner. Lead with what the law bans and what it leaves out. Some protections apply only to minors. netzpolitik's companion commentary ('Eine verpasste Chance', https://netzpolitik.org/2026/digital-fairness-act-eine-verpasste-chance/) is the critical view; mark it as commentary.

stories.label: Brazil Fines Facebook $1.3 Million for Failing to Comply With Court Orders During Election
stories.summary: Brazil's top electoral court has fined Meta's Facebook $1.3 million for not fully complying with takedown orders during the presidential runoff. It is a rare case of a national court enforcing election-period moderation against a US platform. Lead with what Facebook failed to remove and how long it stayed up. Then the precedent: what the fine means next to Meta's revenue, and whether Brazil's enforcement model has teeth. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: A double defense protects photosynthesis from extreme heat
stories.summary: Researchers have identified a two-part mechanism that keeps photosynthesis working under extreme heat. The finding matters because heatwaves already cut crop yields. Lead with the two defenses and the temperatures at which they act, then the stakes: if the mechanism can be bred or engineered into crops and microalgae, harvests in the hottest farming regions, from the Sahel to South Asia, have a path to resilience. Name the journal and the team.

stories.label: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
stories.summary: African swine fever has no approved vaccine or treatment and has killed hundreds of millions of pigs across Asia, Europe and Africa. This paper shows how one viral protein, D250R, sabotages the host cell's protein-tagging machinery to help infection along. Lead with the mechanism in plain terms and why it gives antiviral drug designers a target. Keep the stakes concrete: pork prices and smallholder farmers in China, Vietnam and West Africa.

stories.label: Rezaei: Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Iran's seven conditions are met
stories.summary: The new development since yesterday's seven-conditions story: the IRGC says at least three ships hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and Rezaei now ties reopening the strait itself to Washington's answer. Lead with the mined ships and who crews and insures them; the strait stays shut as leverage while Abu Dhabi talks go on elsewhere. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: UNICEF: 'Drone attacks unlike anything Sudan has seen before'
stories.summary: Drone strikes on Sudan's power stations are cutting children off from water pumps, schools and clinics as drought deepens, UNICEF says; the same day OCHA's annual report counted 71 aid workers killed and 28 injured in Sudan in 2025 amid a funding collapse. Lead with the mechanism — hit the grid and the water stops — and name who flies the drones where the sources do. The people bearing it are the subject.

stories.label: Italy: Hundreds of school evacuated after bomb threats
stories.summary: 312 Italian schools got the same emailed bomb threat at 10 a.m., with matching messages in Northern Ireland, Ireland and Bulgaria. Lead with the coordination across four countries and the cost of a hoax: thousands of children evacuated by one email. Explain why governments are calling it hybrid warfare and what evidence of attribution exists — and say plainly where there is none.

stories.label: Конфискованную у Кольбаева базу отдыха купил не Ширшов, а связанный с Шором фонд. О чем еще соврал президент Жапаров?
stories.summary: OCCRP and Kloop show President Japarov's account of who bought the Bars resort, seized from slain crime boss Kamchy Kolbaev, was false: the buyer was a fund tied to Moldovan fugitive oligarch Ilan Shor, not Bakiyev associate Shirshov. Lead with the lie and the Shor link, days after Japarov filed for the 2027 election. Same day, a Bishkek court gave Baktybek Moldaliev three years for reposting a Kloop article — the cost of reporting this in Kyrgyzstan.

stories.label: Saudis Tell OPEC Output Surged 26% to Highest Since War Began
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia told OPEC it pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, up 26% to the highest since the war began, leading a Gulf output recovery that is pushing Brent crude down even with Hormuz shut. Lead with the mechanism: how Saudi barrels are reaching market around the strait (East-West pipeline to Yanbu, itself struck by the Houthis). The same OPEC report shows Nigeria's output dipping in October — who gains and who loses as prices fall. Name Brent crude.

stories.label: 曝OpenAI三季度收入突破670亿！
stories.summary: OpenAI told investors Q3 revenue hit $10bn (2.6x a year earlier), but its operating loss widened to $10.9bn, and it cut its funding-round valuation from $1.4tn to $1.25tn after the AI share selloff. Lead with the contrast against Anthropic, whose IPO prospectus shows $17bn in the same quarter — 1.7x OpenAI. Mechanism: enterprise and API sales doubled while 91.5% of 1.2bn weekly users still pay nothing.

stories.label: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack
stories.summary: Poland took ePUAP, the national platform citizens use to file official documents and deal with every government agency, offline after a cyberattack. Lead with what millions of Poles cannot do while it is down and the single point of failure a national e-government portal creates. Context: the same day Russia's FSB said it detained Polish spies in Kaliningrad; attribute the attack only as far as officials do.

stories.label: Hongguo is booming. What does that mean for Douyin?
stories.summary: ByteDance's Hongguo short-drama app has a hit AI-made series, Armed Into the Song Dynasty, that has run to about 1,000 episodes in 10 seasons since August, and Douyin's vice president is now warning creators off rushing into AI dramas. Lead with the scale of machine-made serial fiction in China and the tension inside ByteDance between its two apps — the inside view from Chinese tech press.

stories.label: GovTech Deutschland: Gut vernetzt, schlecht durchleuchtet
stories.summary: The German government's answers to a Green Party inquiry confirm that GovTech Deutschland, an industry association, has received public contracts without tender while building its 'Deutschlandplattform' as a rival to the federal Deutschland-Stack. Lead with the accountability gap: who controls the state's digital infrastructure, and how public money reached it without competition.

stories.label: III-nitride device integrates sensing and memory for in-sensor computing
stories.summary: A Nature Materials study reports an aluminium gallium nitride device that detects light at nanowatt-per-square-centimetre levels, stores it and does basic processing in one place, stable up to 300°C. Lead with why that matters: no shuttling data from sensor to memory to chip, in places (engines, space, reactors) where silicon fails. Explain polarization-interface charge control simply.

stories.label: The U.S. may soon lose measles elimination status
stories.summary: The US is close to losing the measles elimination status it has held since 2000, a determination that runs through the Pan American Health Organization once transmission has been continuous for 12 months. Lead with the threshold and the chain of outbreaks behind it, and the vaccination-rate falls that let it happen under Kennedy's HHS. Keep to the epidemiology; Canada already lost its status.

stories.label: Iran lists Argentine Navy, Air Force as terrorist organizations
stories.summary: Tehran designated Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations in retaliation for Buenos Aires blacklisting the IRGC. Lead with the tit-for-tat mechanism: terrorist listings used as reciprocal diplomatic weapons, and Milei's alignment with Washington and Israel pulling a South American state into the Iran war's legal front. Note the AMIA bombing history behind Argentina's IRGC move. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: Russia Says Two Polish Spies Detained in Kaliningrad Region
stories.summary: The FSB says it detained two Polish citizens gathering information on military sites in the Baltic exclave, on the second day of the Abu Dhabi talks and a day after US charges in a UK air-base plot. Attribute the espionage claim to the FSB via Interfax/TASS — it is not established fact. Lead with Kaliningrad's role as the most militarised point on NATO's border and the widening spy-for-spy arrests between Russia and NATO states. Dateline Kaliningrad.

stories.label: Suposta ligação com o crime organizado pode barrar posse de 10 candidatos em 2027
stories.summary: Brazil's electoral prosecutors have asked the TSE to reject eight candidacies, and lawyers are challenging two more, over alleged links to organised crime — ten elected politicians may be barred from taking office in 2027. Lead with the number and the mechanism: how factions like the PCC and militias place candidates, and what legal tool lets the electoral court block a winner. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Doctors on Kennedy's influential preventive care panel have major conflicts of interest, filings reveal
stories.summary: Federal officials granted blanket conflict-of-interest waivers to every member of the US Preventive Services Task Force that Kennedy's HHS remade, letting members with financial stakes vote on which screenings insurers must cover for free. Lead with 'every member' and the mechanism: the panel's recommendations bind insurers under the ACA, so its conflicts reach every insured American. Accountability story. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Spain: Housing crisis prompts general strike
stories.summary: Spain's first general strike in 14 years is over housing, not wages: rents have outrun pay, and the unions CCOO and UGT have shut most industries 18 days before the 29 November election. Lead with the rent-to-income gap and who owns the stock (funds, tourist lets), and why a growth-leading eurozone economy still can't house its workers. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: AD Ports profit jumps 73% due to efforts to mitigate effect of Hormuz closure | The National
stories.summary: AD Ports' Q3 net income rose 73% because the Strait of Hormuz closure pushed cargo onto its overland and alternative-port routes. Lead with who profits from a closed strait: Gulf logistics firms with ports outside Hormuz (Khalifa, Fujairah-linked corridors) capture the rerouted trade while shippers and importers pay. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz as the series.

stories.label: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's tally shows public climate-finance pledges to developing countries down more than 70% as COP31 opens in Antalya. Lead with the 70% and which donors cut most; the cost lands on the climate-vulnerable Global South, including Pakistan, Bangladesh and the Sahel, while rich countries redirect budgets to defence. Advances the COP31 arc with a hard number. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: Why land—a scarce resource—is so important for climate protection
stories.summary: A PIK study in Nature Sustainability quantifies for the first time the trade-off between phasing out fossil fuels and land-based climate measures (forests, farmland, wetlands): leaning on land to offset emissions drives up food and land costs. Lead with the finding on what a balanced policy mix saves, and who bears the cost when land is overused — farmers and food importers in the Global South. Dateline Potsdam.

stories.label: Huawei details how Kirin 9050 runs a 30-billion-parameter model on device
stories.summary: Huawei's sanctioned-supply-chain Kirin 9050 runs a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model (about 2B active) fully offline on a phone, via low-bit quantisation and a new Da Vinci NPU. Lead with the numbers and the mechanism; the structural point is that US export controls pushed Huawei toward on-device efficiency rather than cloud compute. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: 刚刚，腾讯版搜索引擎来了！几乎没广告，能搜公众号
stories.summary: Tencent launched Yuanbao Search, a consumer AI search engine that indexes WeChat official accounts and Channels — content walled off from Baidu — with 'authoritative sources first' ranking across 157 vetted sources and almost no ads. Lead with the walled-garden mechanism: Tencent is turning WeChat's closed content into a search moat against Baidu, and 'authoritative first' in China means state and official media ranked on top. Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: KI-Infrastruktur und Politik: Die neuen Powerplayer bei Meta
stories.summary: Meta has installed a new leadership tier, led by president Dina Powell McCormick, chosen for its ties to the Trump administration, to push AI data-centre and power projects through permitting and politics. Lead with the mechanism: AI infrastructure now depends on political access (land, grid, energy approvals), and Meta is hiring for it. Dateline Menlo Park.

stories.label: US House begins vote on motion to advance impeachment of Pete Hegseth
stories.summary: New since the 11-09 story on Massie's impeachment push: the House has now voted, and the outgoing Republican majority blocked the motion to advance impeachment of Defense Secretary Hegseth over the Iran war. Lead with the vote and who crossed party lines; the mechanism is the lame-duck window — the Democrats who flipped the House last week take their seats in January, when the attempt can return, and Trump lashed out at Massie for breaking ranks.

stories.label: US charges 3 'Iranian-backed' men over alleged plot at UK Fairford air base
stories.summary: US prosecutors have charged three men — one already in prison — they call Iranian-backed operatives over nearly 20 attacks and attempted attacks across the US and Europe, including a plot at RAF Fairford, the British base used in the US war on Iran. Lead with the scale (about 20 incidents) and tie it to the US drawdown from Fairford and Mildenhall already reported; the mechanism is the war's reach into the countries that host its bases. Attribute the 'Iranian-backed' label to prosecutors — these are charges, not convictions.

stories.label: Fire breaks out after drone attack in Ust-Luga port zone -- governor
stories.summary: While Russian and Ukrainian delegations sit in their second day of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, the Leningrad region governor says 141 drones were downed overnight and a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port zone — Russia's main Baltic oil and fuel export terminal. Lead with the timing: the war's biggest long-range strike on Russia's export infrastructure lands during the first peace talks in nine months. Only Russian state news agency TASS reports this: attribute every figure to the governor via TASS. Series: Brent crude.

stories.label: Nayib Bukele, el exembajador Espina y los «brothers in Jesus»
stories.summary: A Redacción Regional investigation reconstructs how Manuel Espina, a former Guatemalan ambassador tied to a CICIG corruption inquiry, opened Washington's doors to Bukele through 'prayer breakfasts' while El Salvador faced international accusations of grave rights abuses — and how the same network links US congressmen, ultraconservatives and the promoters of Próspera, the private city on Roatán suing Honduras for billions. Lead with the mechanism: a religious lobbying channel that buys a rights-abusing government access, and the Próspera claim against the Honduran state.

stories.label: Bonds reel as hot inflation fuels jumbo Fed hike fears
stories.summary: New since yesterday's CPI story: markets now price the risk of a half-point Fed hike in December, not a quarter, after Waller and other Fed speakers turned hawkish — global bonds sold off, the dollar sits near a two-week high and gold slid nearly 3% to around $4,000. Lead with the jump from 25 to 50 basis points and who pays: dollar borrowers in emerging markets and importers whose currencies weaken. Series: the US 10-year Treasury yield, the Fed funds rate, gold, and the yen.

stories.label: Thailand's SCG to reopen Hormuz-affected Vietnam plant in mid-2027
stories.summary: Siam Cement Group's core plastics plant in Vietnam, idled by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, will not restart until mid-2027 as it moves its feedstock away from Middle East naphtha. Lead with the timeline: a war in the Gulf shutting a factory in Ho Chi Minh City for over a year; the mechanism is Southeast Asian petrochemicals' dependence on Gulf feedstock, and what the switch to US ethane costs. Series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent 'confession' email on affair with Singapore-based company's CEO to Nvidia's employees; including his two children
stories.summary: Two new developments in the Huang story: Caixin reports that Alice Huang previously worked at a Shanghai private equity firm alongside a fund manager fined by Chinese securities regulators and now under criminal scrutiny, and the senior Republican on the Senate Banking Committee has called on Jensen Huang to resign (Reuters). Lead with the Caixin finding — mainland reporting adding to a case so far framed from Washington — and the resignation call; do not repeat the market-cap swap already covered. Series: Nvidia shares.

stories.label: 英伟达追投667亿！史上最大IPO启动路演，7名创始人将套现百亿
stories.summary: New since the 11-10 model-release story: Anthropic has launched its IPO roadshow at $70-78 a share, up to $64bn raised and a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4tn, plus a $26bn private placement in which Google and Nvidia take $10bn each and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC the rest. Lead with the circularity: the chipmakers and clouds that sell it compute are buying its shares, against about $895bn in future compute commitments — dwarfing what the IPO raises. Founders keep about 51% of the vote through a special F share. Pricing 18 November, Nasdaq trading 19 November.

stories.label: Restoring social media access comes at a cost in Gabon
stories.summary: Gabon has restored social media after more than eight months of blocking, but on conditions. Lead with what users and platforms had to accept to get access back (registration, content rules, surveillance or platform concessions — whatever the source details); the mechanism is a shutdown used as leverage to rewrite the terms of online speech, a template for other African governments.

stories.label: New study shows COVID value-added tax cut significantly boosted private consumption
stories.summary: A study in the Review of Economic Studies finds Germany's six-month 2020 VAT cut (19% to 16%) significantly raised private spending, most among lower-wealth, younger and middle-aged households, regardless of financial literacy. Lead with who responded; the mechanism is a temporary, pre-announced price cut that pulls purchases forward — evidence relevant to every government now weighing relief against war-driven inflation.

stories.label: Merz accused of 'blackmail' by Slovakian PM after demand for Ukraine aid in EU budget
stories.summary: Germany, the EU's largest net payer, says it will block the bloc's seven-year budget unless it carries a deal on Ukraine aid, and Slovakia's Fico calls that blackmail. Lead with the veto threat: the mechanism is that the budget needs unanimity, so the biggest payer and the smallest holdouts can each hold it hostage. Tie it to the Abu Dhabi talks only as context: Europe is paying for a war whose settlement Washington is negotiating.

stories.label: At least 11 dead after motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria fog
stories.summary: Two pile-ups involving dozens of cars and lorries in dense fog on the Trakia motorway killed at least 11 and injured 46. Lead with the toll; the accountability question is why a main EU freight corridor to Turkey had no fog warning or speed control, and Bulgaria's road deaths, among the highest per head in the EU. A disaster, filed as politics.

stories.label: GOP Taps Combative Jordan as Next House Minority Leader
stories.summary: A decision: after their worst midterm loss in half a century, House Republicans picked hardliner Jim Jordan over the sitting majority leader, while on the other side Sanders and Slotkin said they will not back Schumer for Senate majority leader and Chris Van Hollen, a critic of US arms to Israel and of the Iran war, is calling colleagues to run. Lead with both parties replacing their leaders in one day; the stake for the reader is who will control war powers and Israel arms votes in the new Congress.

stories.label: US Army member arrested in UK over allegations of spying for Russia
stories.summary: British counterterrorism police, working with the FBI and the US military, arrested a serving US soldier in Britain on suspicion of spying for Russia, the same week US aircraft are leaving RAF Mildenhall over Iranian threats. Lead with the arrest and who made it; the mechanism is a joint UK-US case against a soldier on a British base, and what access a US service member in England would have. Dateline: the UK.

stories.label: Matlala seeks to strike investigator's evidence from Madlanga Commission record
stories.summary: On his second day before the Madlanga Commission into police capture, organised-crime accused Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala fought to have the commission investigator's evidence struck from the record. Lead with that tactic; the mechanism is how an accused tries to shrink what an inquiry into police and criminal collusion can rely on, and what the commission's evidence says about South Africa's police leadership.

stories.label: Racial Profiling: Polizei durchsucht in Frankfurt migrantisch gelesene Personen
stories.summary: Frankfurt police have for days been stopping young men they read as migrants, searching their phones and photographing them, and deny it is racial profiling. Lead with the phone searches, which go beyond an ID check; the mechanism is the legal basis that lets police search a phone without suspicion in a designated zone, and who it lands on in a city with a large Muslim population.

stories.label: Microsoft tops Nvidia's market cap for first time since June 2025
stories.summary: New since the stories on Jensen Huang: Nvidia shares fell more than 6% on Tuesday as its board investigates its own CEO over his ties to a suspected Chinese intelligence target, and Microsoft overtook it in market value for the first time since June 2025. Lead with the swap and what drove it: Nvidia's stock and Microsoft's 7.5% rise in a week. Use the Nvidia and Microsoft share prices; do not tie it to SK Hynix unless a source does.

stories.label: NNPC, Oando join global push to end gas flaring as Nigeria's emissions rise
stories.summary: Nigeria's state oil company and Oando signed on to a global oil-and-gas decarbonisation pledge while independent data show the country's gas flaring rose for a third straight year in 2025. Lead with that gap between pledge and record; the mechanism is that flaring burns gas Nigeria could sell or use for power, and the cost lands on Niger Delta communities living beside the flares. Timely with COP31 under way in Antalya.

stories.label: PM Shehbaz stresses clean energy's importance for Pakistan at Chashma-5 nuclear plant event
stories.summary: Pakistan placed the dome on Chashma-5, its Chinese-designed Hualong One reactor near Mianwali, a construction milestone. Lead with what the plant adds to the grid and who built and financed it; the mechanism is Pakistan's bet on Chinese nuclear power to cut a fuel-import bill that the Hormuz closure has made more expensive.

stories.label: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
stories.summary: A researcher found 35,000 apps built with Grok Build, the Musk-owned vibe-coding agent, open to anyone who looked, leaking proprietary business data and secrets, including SpaceXSI's own. Lead with the 35,000; the mechanism is an AI coding tool that publishes what it builds by default, so users ship their secrets without knowing.

stories.label: Japan metals maker plans $1.2bn Malaysia copper foil plant on AI demand
stories.summary: Mitsui Kinzoku will spend 190 billion yen ($1.2bn) on a copper foil factory in Malaysia, the ultra-thin copper that goes into AI server circuit boards. Lead with Malaysia winning a choke-point AI input; the mechanism is that the AI build-out runs on materials few firms make, and copper demand follows it. Series: copper and the yen.

stories.label: Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production - Nature Sustainability
stories.summary: Researchers reconstruct how early-20th-century copper smelting spread heavy-metal pollution across North America, recorded in ice and sediment, and estimate its health toll. Lead with the scale of the footprint and the deaths it implies; the mechanism is how smelter emissions travelled continent-wide, a lesson for today's copper boom driven by AI and electrification.

stories.label: Dual-layer engineering of herbicide resistance in crops - Nature Biotechnology
stories.summary: Zhang and colleagues (Nature Plants) engineer herbicide resistance in crops at two layers, the protein and the gene's regulation, so the trait holds up where single edits fail. Lead with why resistance traits break down; the mechanism is two-layer editing, and the stake is who controls these traits and what more herbicide-tolerant crops mean for weeds and farmers.
